data.sourceWord: MCQ: Which of the following gives the meaning of anatta?
data.targetWord: No fixed self

examples.en-GB: Answer: No fixed self | Distractors: Impermanence; Suffering; Teaching

data.targetWord: The Five Aggregates (skandhas) include Form (rupa — the physical body) and Sensation (vedana — feelings that arise when we come into contact with things).
Perception (samjna) refers to recognising what things are; Consciousness (vijnana) refers to a person's general awareness of the world.
Right Speech influences Buddhists to speak truthfully, never lie, and avoid gossip or slander, promoting kindness and non-harm through their words.
Right Speech encourages Buddhists to avoid perjury, exaggeration, and lustful speech, living by the Five Precepts and acting in ways that help rather than harm.
Nibbana literally means 'extinction' — the snuffing out of the three poisons of greed, hate and ignorance. It is the goal of the Buddhist faith and can be reached in this life or after death.

Nibbana marks the end of the cycle of rebirth (samsara). The Buddha attained Nibbana at enlightenment and Parinibbana at death. In Mahayana Buddhism, a Bodhisattva may delay their own Nibbana to help others.
'One road leads to wealth; another road leads to nirvana. Let the mendicant, the disciple of Buddha, learn this and not strive for honour but seek wisdom.' (Dhammapada ch.5, v.75)

data.sourceWord: MCQ: Why is the Buddha known as the First Refuge?
data.targetWord: Buddhists see the Buddha as the perfect example of wisdom and compassion to follow.

examples.en-GB: Answer: Buddhists see the Buddha as the perfect example of wisdom and compassion to follow. | Distractors: Buddhists believe the Buddha is a creator who controls the universe.; Buddhists believe the Buddha removes bad karma from believers.; Buddhists see the Buddha as the guardian of sacred temples.

data.sourceWord: FOR: Buddha gained enlightenment — proof the path works
data.targetWord: The historical Buddha gained enlightenment in his lifetime, proving his teachings lead to their goal. His life is therefore the most reliable guide for Buddhists seeking enlightenment themselves.

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: The Pali Canon was written 500 years later
data.targetWord: The Pali Canon recording the Buddha's life was written 500 years after his death. We cannot be certain it is historically accurate, which undermines using his example as an absolute guide.

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: His lifestyle is impossible in the modern world
data.targetWord: The Buddha lived an extreme life — 29 years in a palace, 6 as an ascetic, leaving his wife and child. This is impractical for most modern Buddhists; the Dhamma itself may be a better guide.

data.sourceWord: MCQ: Which one is NOT one of the Five Moral Precepts?
data.targetWord: Do not be jealous

examples.en-GB: Answer: Do not be jealous | Distractors: Do not take life; Do not take what is not given; Do not speak falsehoods

data.sourceWord: Wesak — Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and death (parinirvana)
data.targetWord: Wesak commemorates the Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and death (parinirvana) — the three most significant events in his life, celebrated with lanterns, gifts, and acts of dana.

examples.en-GB: AQA Q2.2 — events remembered at Wesak

data.targetWord: Wesak remembers the Buddha's death and passing into final parinirvana — the complete extinction of the flame of existence and entry into ultimate Nibbana.

data.targetWord: Buddhist shrines provide a focal point for meditation and concentration; the Buddharupa helps Buddhists direct their mind and deepen their practice of samatha or vipassana.
Offerings at shrines carry symbolic meaning: candles represent wisdom, flowers remind of impermanence, and incense symbolises purity — reinforcing Buddhist values with each act of worship.

data.sourceWord: Samatha meditation — developing a calm mind
data.targetWord: Samatha meditation develops a calm, focused mind by concentrating on breathing. It prepares the mind for vipassana meditation, reduces restlessness, and is said to be suitable for all people.

data.sourceWord: Samatha meditation — part of the Eightfold Path
data.targetWord: Samatha meditation is central to the last three stages of the Eightfold Path (Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration) and one of the six perfections in the Mahayana tradition.
'He who is mentally concentrated, sees things according to reality.' (The Buddha) — showing how samatha meditation brings insight into the true nature of existence.
The six Mahayana perfections (paramitas): generosity, morality, patience, energy, meditation, wisdom — qualities a bodhisattva cultivates on the path to enlightenment.

data.sourceWord: AGAINST: Six perfections — ideals that are hard to achieve
data.targetWord: Being called 'perfections' immediately makes them difficult — they are ideals. Enlightenment may take many lifetimes, and cultivating energy (virya) or wisdom (prajna) is too hard for many people.

data.sourceWord: FOR: Six perfections — compassionate framework for all
data.targetWord: The six perfections are based on compassion and universal moral principles that are compatible with any society. All Buddhists have the potential to cultivate generosity, morality, patience, energy, meditation, and wisdom step by step.

data.answer: Anatta means there is no fixed self.

data.prompt: What is the goal of the Buddhist faith?
data.answer: Nibbana is the goal of the Buddhist faith.

data.prompt: What do Buddhists celebrate at Wesak?
data.answer: Wesak celebrates the birth, enlightenment and death of the Buddha.

data.title: The Three Jewels of Buddhism
data.sourcePassage: The Three Jewels, or Three Refuges, lie at the heart of Buddhist practice. They are the Buddha, the Dhamma (his teachings), and the Sangha (the community of practitioners). Taking refuge in the Three Jewels is the formal way of becoming a Buddhist. The Buddha is the historical teacher who attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree and spent 45 years teaching others the path to liberation. The Dhamma refers to his teachings, preserved in texts such as the Pali Canon, including the Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path. The Sangha is the community of monks, nuns and lay followers who preserve and transmit the teachings. Buddhists believe that by taking refuge in all three, they have the support they need to progress toward Nibbana — the end of suffering and the cycle of rebirth. The concept of anatta (no fixed self) and anicca (impermanence) are central to understanding why the path is necessary.
